name: Announcements
description: I want an Announcements App that posts my GitHub releases to Mastodon. A Project is one of my repositories, identified by its owner/name, with optional hashtags and a sentence about what it is; Projects are all mine, I add them by hand on a list. An Account is my Mastodon account, identified by its name (like @me@mastodon.example), with the address to post to and an access token kept encrypted; also all mine, added by hand on its own list. A Release is a release the pipeline found, identified by its URL, with its title, its Project, when it was published, the drafted post, when it was posted and a link to the post. Releases have stages: they start drafted, and can become posted (by me or the pipeline) or skipped (by me only); I can bring a skipped one back to drafted. No report pages. When installed it needs an LLM for drafting, my Projects and my Account. One pipeline, Announce, runs every hour, and the Releases list has a "Check now" button that runs it too. It reads my Projects, fetches each one's release feed from github.com, keeps releases published in the last three days that it hasn't seen before, and, only if I have an Account, has the LLM draft a short friendly post of at most 450 characters with the version, what's new, the link and the hashtags. It saves each as a drafted Release, then posts it to my first Account's post address with its token; each post waits for my approval, where I can edit the text. Once posted, the Release is marked posted with the time and the post's link. At most 10 posts a day.
notes: Only github.com is allowed as a domain in the policy (the Mastodon server is approved at the gate the first time). Each feed is read for at most 5 items.

name: Apartments
description: I'm looking for a flat to rent and want an Apartments App. A Search is what I'm looking for, identified by its name: areas, a maximum price, minimum rooms, must-haves and whether I'm still looking; Searches are all mine. An Agent is an agent or owner I write to, identified by name, with an email, agency, phone and notes on when I can visit; all mine too. A Listing is a flat a pipeline found, identified by its URL, with title, price, area, rooms, size, floor, agency, and how well it fits (match, maybe or no) with the reason. On a Listing the agent's name, the viewing time and my notes are mine. Listings have stages: new, favorite, contacted, viewing, offer, rejected. They start new. Me or a pipeline can move new to rejected, favorite to contacted, and new, favorite or contacted to viewing; only I move new or rejected to favorite, viewing to offer, favorite/contacted/viewing/offer to rejected, and rejected back to new. A listing's page shows its price history. No report pages. It needs a recipe for listings.example/rent, my Searches, an LLM, Telegram, an email account and Google Calendar. Pipelines: Listings runs every day at 8:00, 13:00 and 19:00: it reads the site (center and north districts) with the recipe, records each price, has the LLM mark new listings against my active Searches and saves them (a "no" starts rejected), then tells me on Telegram about new matches and about price drops on listings I'm favoriting, contacted, viewing or offered on. Ask for a viewing: a button on a favorite listing's page (asks me first) drafts an email to the Agent I named on the listing, using their address only, sends it after my approval where I can edit it, and moves the listing to contacted; at most 10 emails a day. Viewing: when I set a listing's viewing time in the future, a 45-minute calendar event waits for my approval and the listing moves to viewing. Compare favorites: a button on the list has the LLM compare and rank up to 10 favorites against what I look for, sent on Telegram.
notes: The Search and Agent lists have no explicit add: true, although both types are mine and the setup says Searches are added on their page. The recipe reads at most 300 items. Only listings.example is an allowed domain. The Listings list also has a "Check now" button running Listings.

name: Bills
description: I want a Bills App that reads my bills from email. A Bill is identified by a key made of the sender's domain with the bill's reference, period or due date, so the same bill arriving again stays one Bill. It has the issuer, the sender, an amount of money with its currency, the due date, the month it's for, the period, the reference, and the email's sender address and subject. Bills aren't mine: the pipeline writes them, and I don't type any of their fields. Bills have stages: they start due, I mark them paid, and I can move a paid one back to due. No report pages; the list groups bills by month with totals. When installed it needs an email account, an LLM, Google Calendar and Telegram. One pipeline, Read bills, runs every day at 8:00 and 18:00: it fetches my emails from the last 7 days, picks out the bills (invoices, utility or phone bills, payment requests with an amount for me to pay), reads each one from the text or an attached PDF, and saves them. For each new bill it puts a 15-minute reminder in my calendar 3 days before it's due, which waits for my approval, and if a bill is 30% or more higher than usual it tells me on Telegram. Nothing is ever paid.
notes: The list highlights due dates within 3 days unless paid, and totals the amount and the unpaid amount per month: page detail a person would rarely state.

name: Car
description: I want a Car App for my car's papers and services. A Vehicle is identified by its name (like "Family car"), with its plate, model, year, current mileage in km and notes. A Paper is identified by its name (like "Family car insurance"), with the vehicle's name, its kind (insurance, inspection, vignette, tax, registration, licence, service or other), the date it runs out, the km a service is due at, its cost, the provider and notes. Both Vehicles and Papers are entirely mine: I type them all in and no pipeline writes them. No stages and no report pages. The papers list shows what runs out within 30 days, grouped by vehicle. No LLM. When installed it needs my Papers, Telegram and Google Calendar. Pipelines: Papers due runs every day at 8:00. It reads my Papers and Vehicles and tells me on Telegram once when a paper has 30 days left, once more when it has 7 days left, once when a service is less than 1,000 km away according to the vehicle's mileage, and once when I renew a paper (move its date on). Each warning is sent only once, not every day. Paper in calendar: when I add a Paper or change the date it runs out, it puts a 30-minute event at 9:00 on that day in my calendar, after my approval; a date already past does nothing.
notes: The Paper and Vehicle lists have no explicit add: true, although both types are mine and the setup says Papers are added on their page.

name: Clients
description: I freelance and want a Clients App. A Client is identified by name, with an email, company, rate and notes; Clients are all mine, and their address is the only one emails go to. A Lead is an inquiry from email, identified by its email thread so a reply updates the same Lead, with title, sender, summary, budget, deadline, which client it looks like, a score and the reason. On a Lead, the client's name and my notes are mine. Lead stages: new, qualified, proposal, won, lost; it starts new. I move new to qualified or lost, qualified or proposal to won or lost, proposal/won/lost back to qualified, and qualified or lost back to new; qualified to proposal is made by me or a pipeline. An Invoice is identified by its lead, one per won lead, with a number, client, title, the quoted budget, issue and due dates; the amount is mine. Invoice stages: draft, sent, overdue, paid; it starts draft. I move draft to sent, sent or overdue to paid, and sent/overdue/paid back to draft or sent; sent to overdue is me or a pipeline. No report pages. It needs my Clients, an email account, an LLM and Telegram. Pipelines: Inquiries runs every 15 minutes, picks out emails asking me for paid work from the last 7 days, has the LLM summarize and score each against the work I take, saves them as Leads and tells me about new ones on Telegram. Proposal: a "Send proposal" button on a qualified Lead (asks first) drafts a proposal to the Client I named on it, sent to that Client's email in the same thread after my approval, where I can edit it; the Lead moves to proposal. Lead won: when a Lead moves to won, an Invoice draft due in 14 days is made and I'm told on Telegram. Overdue invoices: every weekday at 9:00, sent invoices past due move to overdue and I'm told. Payment reminder: a "Payment reminder" button on an overdue Invoice (asks first) emails a polite reminder to its Client after my approval. Each email pipeline sends at most 10 a day.
notes: The Client list has no explicit add: true, although Client is mine and the setup says clients are added on its page. Invoice numbers are generated as INV-<date>-<4 chars of the thread>.

name: Follow-ups
description: I want a Follow-ups App for emails I sent that nobody answered. A FollowUp is one such email thread, identified by its thread id, with the subject, who it went to, when I sent it, how many days it's been waiting, how many nudges went and when the last one did. The pipelines write them; only my notes on a FollowUp are mine. Stages: waiting, nudged, snoozed, dropped; it starts waiting. Only the pipeline moves waiting to nudged. Me or a pipeline can move waiting or nudged to snoozed, and snoozed back to waiting. Only I move waiting, nudged or snoozed to dropped, dropped back to waiting, and nudged back to waiting. No report pages. When installed it needs just an email account. Pipelines: Follow-ups runs every Monday at 9:00, and the Waiting list has a "Nudge now" button (asks first). It finds my sent emails with no answer after 5 days, from the last 45 days, with at most two nudges each, skips the ones I snoozed or dropped, lists them, and drafts a short friendly nudge for each in its thread and language. All the nudges wait for my approval together as one batch: I untick the ones I don't want. Each approved one is sent from the account the email went from and its row becomes nudged; each unticked one becomes snoozed. At most 20 emails a day. Snooze: when a FollowUp is snoozed, it schedules Wake for two weeks later (snoozing again restarts the two weeks). Wake: two weeks after, if the row is still snoozed, it moves back to waiting.
notes: The email search returns at most 20 threads per run. Wake is started only by Snooze's delayed run, not by a schedule or a button.

name: Hiring
description:
I want a Hiring App. A Role is a job I'm hiring for, and I type all of them in myself on a Roles list where I can add one: each Role is known by its name, with a description of the work, what an applicant must have, and whether it's closed. A Candidate is someone who applied by email, known by an id (their application email's message id), with their name, email address, the Role they apply for, a score, why that score, a short summary, their CV as a file, and when they applied; the notes on a Candidate are mine. A Candidate starts as new. Me or a pipeline can move them from new to invited, and from new or invited to rejected; only I move invited to hired, and I can move rejected or hired back to new. No report page. It needs an email account where the applications arrive, and my Roles.

The Applications pipeline runs on working days at 17:00, and from a "Check now" button on the Candidates list. If I have any open Roles, it reads the new emails and keeps only job applications (not recruiters offering me people or jobs). For each one it keeps the attached CV, saves the applicant as a new Candidate, reads the CV, works out their name, which open Role they apply for and a short summary, and scores them from 0 to 100 against that Role (0 when none fits). Then the day's applicants come to me, best first, and I pick who to invite. Each one I pick gets a warm interview invitation written for them, and everyone else gets a short kind no; both go as replies in the applicant's own thread, to their address, and each wait for my approval as a batch (I can untick one). Each email sent moves its Candidate to invited or rejected. At most 60 emails a day.
notes: Only open Roles (not closed) are read. Only PDF, Word or text CVs are read; up to 3 attachments kept per email. The invitation asks for two or three times next week for a 45-minute video call; the decline text is fixed. The 'Check now' button asks for confirmation first. Candidates are saved twice (first without score, then scored).

name: Job Search
description:
I want a Job Search App with one type, a Job: a job posting, known by its address (url), with its title, company, location, when it was posted (as text), a description, a score and why, the source it came from and an external id; the comments on a Job are mine. Its stages are new, shortlisted, skipped, prepared, applied, responded, interview, offer and rejected, and a Job starts as new. Me or a pipeline can move it from new to shortlisted or skipped; from new, shortlisted or skipped to prepared or applied; from prepared to applied; from applied to responded, interview or rejected; from responded to interview or rejected; and from interview to offer or rejected. Only I move shortlisted and skipped between new, shortlisted and skipped, move prepared back to shortlisted or skipped, and move freely among applied, responded, interview, offer and rejected to undo a mistake. Jobs have a report page: how many were found, shortlisted, applied, got a reply, interviews and rejections, a weekly trend, and tables by score band and by source. It needs a job board's recipe, jobs.example.com/search, the LLM, Telegram, and an email account.

The Job board pipeline runs every weekday at 8:00: it reads the back-end and full-stack categories of jobs.example.com with that recipe (up to 300 postings), keeps only the ones not kept before, sets aside recruitment agencies as skipped Jobs, scores the rest against what I look for (a senior or lead back-end or full-stack TypeScript or Node.js role, remote or hybrid, at a product company; no on-call heavy roles or short contracts), learning from how my applications went, and saves them as Jobs. It tells me on Telegram about each new one scored 70 or more. It may only visit jobs.example.com.

The Application replies pipeline runs every 15 minutes: it reads my inbox's new emails, keeps the ones where an employer or recruiter writes about a job I applied for, moves that Job on from what the email says, and when its status changed tells me on Telegram.
notes: The list page groups by status with moves; the report periods are 90, 30 and 365 days. Neither pipeline sends anything, so no approvals. The 'Move them here' migration mentioned in the header comment is not in the file.

name: Lockbox
description:
I want a Lockbox App that keeps my projects' GitHub variables and secrets and sends them to GitHub when I press Sync. Everything in it is mine: I type it all in, pipelines never write it. A Project is known by its name, with a description; I add them on a Projects list. A GitHubOwner is a GitHub user or organization, known by its name, with its kind (user or organization) and a token, a credential for api.github.com. A Path is a place in a project for its values, like /backend-api or /_backend for shared ones; Storm makes its key, and it has its project and name; I add them on the project's page. An Entry is a variable or a secret, with a key Storm makes: its name, kind (variable or secret), project, path of that project, environment (production, staging or development), and a value for a variable or an encrypted secret that is never shown again; I add them on an Entries list and from the project's page. A Bundle, known by its name and added on a Bundles list, says where one environment of a project goes: its project, environment, its paths in order (a later path's value of a name wins), a destination (repository, environment, organization or dependabot), its GitHub owner, and the repository, the GitHub environment or the visibility (all or private) as the destination needs. No stages, no report pages. It needs a GitHub owner with its token, and my entries and a Bundle.

The Sync pipeline starts from a "Sync" button on a Bundle's page. It takes the Bundle's GitHub owner and its token, works out the GitHub address from the destination, reads the Entries of the Bundle's project and environment on its paths, one per name with the last path winning, then encrypts each secret with GitHub's public key and puts it, and creates or updates each variable. It never deletes anything, one failure doesn't stop the others, and it only talks to api.github.com.
notes: Pressing Sync is meant to be the approval (the pipeline's 'Act without asking when I start it' switch), so the GitHub writes otherwise wait at the gate; hard to say plainly. GitHub owners' list has no add button (owners are added via the setup/credential). An organization bundle must have an organization owner, else it errors. Variables already on GitHub are found up to 120. Path and Entry 'path' fields are limited to the chosen project's paths.

name: Meetings
description:
I want a Meetings App. A Meeting is a request to meet someone emailed me, known by its email thread, with its subject, who it's with and their email, when I proposed times, when I nudged them, when the meeting is, and a link to the event; the notes are mine. A Meeting starts as proposed; me or a pipeline can move it to booked; only I move proposed or booked to dropped, and dropped back to proposed. No report page. It needs an email account to read the requests and answer them, and Google Calendar for my free times and the events.

The Meetings pipeline runs every 15 minutes, and from a "Check now" button on the Meetings list. It reads the new emails. For a new email where someone personally asks to meet or find a time (not an invitation with a time already set), it looks at my calendar's busy times and drafts a reply proposing three free times on the next working days, Monday to Friday between 9:00 and 17:00, asking which suits them; the reply goes to the sender in their thread after I approve it, and once sent it's a proposed Meeting. For an answer in a proposed Meeting's thread, it works out the time they chose and creates a 30-minute calendar event with them invited and a Meet link, after I approve it; created, the Meeting is booked. If they answered without choosing a time, it tells me on Telegram. At most 20 emails and 20 events a day.

The Meeting nudge pipeline runs on working days at 9:00: each proposed Meeting whose email got no answer in 3 days gets one nudge in its thread, to the person I wrote to, kindly asking which time suits them; the day's nudges wait for my approval as one batch, and each sent one records when I nudged. At most 20 emails a day.
notes: Telegram is used by the Meetings pipeline but not listed in setup. Only one nudge ever per thread; looks back 30 days. Video call unless they asked to meet in person.

name: Memos
description:
I want a Memos App for notes to keep. A Memo has a key Storm makes, so its title can change, and has a title, some text, a photo if I like, and tags (a list of words). I add memos by hand on the Memos list, newest first, searchable by title, text and tags, with the tags as chips to filter by and a calendar of the days memos were kept. No stages and no report page. It needs Telegram, for /memo, though the page works without it.

The From Telegram pipeline starts with the /memo command on Telegram: the text after it becomes a memo, its first line (without the #tags) as the title, and every #word as a tag; a photo sent with /memo as its caption is kept with it (a photo alone is titled by its day). It saves the Memo and replies on Telegram with "Kept:" and its title.
notes: Memo is not a mine type (the Telegram pipeline writes it) but the list has add. Title is cut to 80 characters.

name: Newsletter
description:
I want a Newsletter App. A Subscriber is someone who gets it, typed in by me on a Subscribers list: known by their email, with a name to greet them by and the date they subscribed. A Feed is an RSS or Atom feed I collect links from, also mine, added on a Feeds list: known by its address, with a name and whether it's paused. A Link is a link seen this week, known by its address, with a title, its source, when it was found, a summary and which issue used it; my note on it is mine. A Link starts as new; me or a pipeline move it to used or skipped, and only I move it back to new. An Issue is an issue written, known by its date as id, with a title, how many links and recipients, when it was sent and its text; it starts as drafted and only a pipeline moves it to sent. Unsubscribed is an address that replied "unsubscribe", known by its email, with when it asked. No report pages. It needs an email account to read my forwarded links and send the issue, the LLM, my Subscribers, and a text setting: my newsletter's name.

The Collect links pipeline runs every three hours, and from a "Collect now" button on the Links list. It reads the new emails and my Feeds that aren't paused: an email with #link in its subject gives its first link, a feed its items of the last week; ones not seen before are saved as new Links. A reply whose first line says "unsubscribe" saves its sender as Unsubscribed. Nothing is sent.

The Write the issue pipeline runs on Friday at 9:00, and from a "Write the issue now" button on the Links list. The week's new Links come to me to pick; the issue is written from the ones I pick, using my note on each, and kept as an Issue. Then one email to each Subscriber who hasn't unsubscribed, greeting them by name and saying how to stop, waits for my approval as one batch. Once sent, the Issue is sent, the picked Links used and the rest skipped. At most 200 emails a day.
notes: Each feed is read on its own and one failing doesn't stop the others. The issue's title is the newsletter name plus the date.

name: Orders from shop emails
description:
I'd like an Orders App that keeps track of what I buy online, from the shops' emails. Each thing is an Order, identified by the shop's email domain together with the order number, so every email about the same order adds to the same Order. It keeps the shop, the order number, what I bought, the total (an amount of money) and its currency, the order date, the delivery date, the last day to return it, the tracking number and tracking link, and the sender and subject of the email. Two fields are mine: Keep (yes or no) and my notes. Orders only come from emails; I don't add them by hand.

An Order goes through stages: it starts as ordered, then shipped, delivered, returning, returned or cancelled. From ordered it can go to shipped, delivered or cancelled; from shipped to delivered or cancelled; from delivered to returning or returned; from returning to returned. All of those moves can be made by me or by a pipeline. Only I can move a returning, returned or cancelled order back to delivered, to undo a mistake.

It needs an email account, the LLM and Telegram.

Pipelines:
- Every 30 minutes, read the last week's emails, keep only the ones about my orders (confirmations, shipping, delivery, refunds, cancellations; not offers or newsletters), have the LLM read the details, and merge each into its Order, moving its stage forward (a refund means returned). If delivered without a return date, give it 14 days from delivery. Tell me each change on Telegram. Nothing is sent.
- Whenever an Order changes: if it is delivered and not marked Keep, schedule a reminder for 9:00 three days before its return date; cancel it once the order is returning, returned or cancelled, or I mark Keep.
- That reminder tells me on Telegram what the order is and until when I can return it.
- A "Return it" button on a delivered order: the LLM drafts a return request to the shop, the order moves to returning, and I get the draft on Telegram to send myself.
notes: The return reminder moves with the return date (keyed per order), and when the reminder time is already past but the return date is not, it fires about ten minutes later. The list groups orders by month with totals and flags return dates due within 3 days unless kept. The undo move has no explicit 'by' (default).

name: Papers: receipts, warranties, contracts
description:
I want a Papers App for my receipts, invoices, warranties and contracts, each with its photo or PDF. Each one is a Paper, with a key Storm makes for it; I add them by hand on a list. A Paper has a title, the document, what kind it is (receipt, invoice, warranty, contract or other), the merchant, an amount of money and its currency, a date, a category (office, equipment, software, travel, meals, services, personal or other), a warranty end date, and for contracts an end date and the notice in days, plus notes. One field is mine: Write to, the Merchant that claims and cancellations go to. Merchants are all mine: I type them in (a name, which identifies each, an email address and notes) on their own list with add. No stages, no report pages.

It also uses the Bill type from my Bills App (issuer, amount, currency, due date, month, status), but works without one.

It needs the LLM, Google Calendar, an email account and Telegram.

Pipelines:
- When a paper's document is added or changed, the LLM reads it and fills in the kind, merchant, amount, currency, date, category, warranty end, contract end and notice.
- When a paper's warranty end changes, put that day in my calendar at 9:00, after I approve it; a past date does nothing.
- A Telegram command /paper with a photo or PDF and its title as caption keeps it as a new Paper and tells me; if there's no file, it says so.
- A "Claim warranty" button on a receipt or warranty: the LLM drafts a claim and emails it, with the document attached, to the paper's Write to merchant, after I approve and edit it. At most 10 a day. With no merchant set, it tells me on Telegram.
- A "Cancel contract" button on a contract: the same, a cancellation notice to its merchant after I approve. At most 10 a day.
- Whenever a paper changes: a contract with an end date gets a Telegram reminder at 9:00 two weeks before its notice runs out (30 days before its end without a notice), cancelled when it's no longer a contract or has no end.
- On the 1st of every month at 8:00, and from an "Expense report" button on the list: last month's receipts and invoices (not personal ones) and last month's bills; I untick what isn't an expense, then one email with each and the totals per currency, the documents attached, goes to my accountant's address (a setting), after I approve it. At most 3 a day.
notes: The expense report attaches at most 20 documents, 18 MB together (a step rule, not a limits entry). Values I typed stay over what the LLM reads. The contract reminder moves with the dates and fires about ten minutes later when its time is already past. The list flags warranty ends within 30 days and contract ends within 60.

name: Prices watched across shops
description:
I'd like a Prices App to watch the prices of products across shops. A Product is all mine: I type each in, identified by its name, with a target price (an amount of money) and its currency, whether it's watched (yes or no), and a list of its shops, one shop page address per line with the variant after a "|". Pipelines only read Products. An Offer is what one shop's page says about a product, identified by the product, the shop's address and the variant together: the product, the shop, the address, the variant, the price and currency, whether it's in stock, the page's title, any problem reading it, and when it was checked. Offers are written by the pipeline; each one's page shows its price history. No stages, no report pages.

It needs my products added on their page, and Telegram.

One pipeline, every day at 9:00: check every watched product at each of its shops and tell me on Telegram only what's new: a shop at or under my target (once), the lowest price in 90 days, or back in stock, naming the cheapest shop. If some pages couldn't be read, tell me that on Telegram too.
notes: The Product list page has no add option in the file even though Products are added by hand (setup kind 'entities'). Offers are grouped by product, sorted by price, and removed ones shown. The header comment mentions migrating from the old Prices page, which is not part of the App's behaviour.

name: Quotes from suppliers
description:
I want a Quotes App for asking my suppliers for quotes and comparing them. A Supplier is all mine: I type them in on a list with add, each identified by its name, with an email address, what they supply, and notes. A Request is also all mine, added on a list: what I need (identified by a key Storm makes), its details, when I need it by, and which Suppliers to ask. A Quote is a supplier's answer to a request, written by the pipelines and identified by the request and the supplier: the request, the supplier, the price, currency, delivery date, terms, and when it was asked and answered. A Quote starts as asked; a pipeline moves it from asked to quoted, and from asked or quoted to accepted or declined; I can move an accepted or declined one back to quoted. A request's page shows its quotes side by side. No report pages.

It needs an email account and my suppliers with their email addresses.

Pipelines:
- An "Ask for quotes" button on a request: email the request to each of its suppliers, at their address from my Suppliers, all approved by me as one batch; each one sent becomes a Quote, asked. At most 30 emails a day.
- Every 30 minutes, read new emails; a reply in a request's thread is read by the LLM for the price, currency, delivery date and terms, saved into its Quote as quoted, and I'm told on Telegram. Nothing is sent.
- An "Accept" button on a quoted Quote: an acceptance email to that supplier and a thank-you to the request's other suppliers, each after my approval, all to the addresses in my Suppliers; then that Quote is accepted and the others declined. At most 30 emails a day.
notes: Setup lists only email and the Suppliers, yet quote-read also sends a Telegram message. A Quote's key is the request id joined with the supplier's name. A Quote is only saved as accepted or declined when its email actually went out.

name: Releases to read (starter)
description:
Make me a simple Releases to read App, a starter that needs nothing set up: no accounts, no LLM, no messages. It keeps new releases of a few open-source projects (Node.js, VS Code and Prisma on GitHub) from their public release feeds. Each is a Release, identified by the feed entry's id, with its title, when it was published, its link and the project. My notes on it are mine. Releases come only from the feeds; I don't add them by hand.

A Release starts as new, and I mark it read or skipped right on its row; I can also move a read or skipped one back to new. No report pages.

One pipeline, every day at 9:00 and from a "Check now" button on the list: read the projects' release feeds and keep each release; one seen before is left as it is, so the stage I gave it stays.
notes: The feeds are fixed GitHub release Atom URLs (allowed domain github.com); the read takes at most 30 entries.

name: Releases of my server's stack
description:
I want a Releases App for the releases of what runs on my server. Each is a Release, identified by the feed entry's id, with its title, when it was published, its link, the feed it came from, and a summary. Whether I've upgraded (yes or no) is mine. Releases come only from the feeds; I don't add them by hand. No stages, no report pages.

It needs the LLM and Telegram.

Pipelines:
- Watch, every day at 9:00 and from a "Check now" button on the list: read the release feeds of my stack (Node.js, Prisma, Playwright, Caddy, pgvector, pg-boss, n8n, Paperless-ngx, Memos and Tailscale on GitHub, and the PostgreSQL news feed), keep each release, and only for the ones not seen before have the LLM write one line per project and version on what matters when upgrading (security fixes, breaking changes, migrations), sent to me on Telegram. Nothing on a quiet day.
- Notes, from an "Upgrade notes" button on a release's page: the LLM summarizes what upgrading to it means, sent to me on Telegram.
- Failed run issue, when the Watch pipeline fails: open an issue in my GitHub repository saying what went wrong, only after I approve it. It needs a GitHub API key credential and the repository (owner/name) as a text setting.
notes: The feed list and allowed domains (github.com, www.postgresql.org) are fixed in the pipeline; the summary is capped at 300 words and the notes at 200. The issue gets the label 'storm'. The App's summary field on each Release is never written by a pipeline (only the Telegram message carries it).

name: Server ops: monitors, incidents, fixes and GitHub issues
description:
I want a Server ops App for my monitors and incidents on what I run, no LLM. A Monitor is identified by its name and I add them on a list. Its kind (http, tcp or ping), address, host, port, expected status, ignore certificate errors, paused, and the Repository its issues go to are mine; the checks fill in its status (up or down), response time, why it's down, when it was checked and until when its certificate is valid. An Incident is identified by an id made of what it is about and when it started; only its notes are mine. Its stages: it starts open, then acknowledged, then resolved. Open to acknowledged, and open or acknowledged to resolved, by me or a pipeline; acknowledged or resolved back to open. Three types are entirely mine, each by name, added by hand: a Runbook (a webhook that fixes one monitor: method, address, an encrypted authorization header), a GitHubOwner (a user or organization with its GitHub token) and a Repository (owner/name; one may be the default). On install it needs a database credential (a read-only user), and Telegram.

Pipelines:
- Check monitors: every five minutes, and a 'Check now' button on the Monitors list. Checks each monitor that isn't paused, keeps its status and a response time history, opens an Incident when one goes down and resolves it with how many minutes it lasted when it's back up, telling me on Telegram.
- Monitor alerts: the same from an outside monitor's webhook (with a token).
- Database check: every 10 minutes, and a 'Check the database now' button on Incidents. Runs counting queries on the database; a check above 0 opens an Incident, back at 0 resolves it and the connection incident; tells me on Telegram.
- Database down: when Database check fails, one connection Incident if none is open, on Telegram.
- Incident issue: an 'Open issue' button on an open Incident. A GitHub issue in its monitor's repository, else the default one, with that owner's token, sent only after I approve; then the Incident is acknowledged with the issue's link. If something is missing, Telegram says what to add.
- Offer a fix: when an Incident opens, each of its monitor's runbooks is called only after I approve; Telegram says what each answered, and the Incident is acknowledged. At most 20 requests a day.
- Fix: a 'Fix' button on an open or acknowledged Incident, the same, at most 20 requests a day; says so when there is no runbook.
- Week: every Monday at 9:00, last week's incidents in numbers on Telegram.
notes: The Monitor list's 'Check now' and the Incident list's 'Check the database now' buttons run schedule-triggered pipelines (no separate trigger). The database-check SQL (orders/jobs) is an example to replace. Repository and GitHubOwner have no title field; GitHubOwner token is a credential for api.github.com. Monitor alerts accepts Uptime Kuma's and a plain JSON body. Runbooks: at most 5 per monitor read. Incident form edits only notes.

name: Subscriptions from email, with reminders and a review
description:
I want a Subscriptions App: the services I pay for again and again, read from their emails. Each Subscription is identified by the service's name in lowercase letters and digits, so every email about the same service updates the same one. It has the plan, price and currency, period (weekly, monthly, yearly, other), what it costs a month, last charged, next renewal, trial end, and the email's sender and subject. Only the notes are mine (how much I use it). Stages: trial, active (where it starts), cancelling, cancelled. Trial to active or cancelled, active to cancelling or cancelled, cancelling to cancelled, and cancelled back to trial or active, each by me or a pipeline; cancelling back to active too. It needs an email account, the LLM and Telegram.

Pipelines:
- Read emails: every 2 hours, reads the last month's emails, keeps the ones about subscriptions (trials, receipts, renewals, price changes, cancellations), reads each into its Subscription with the monthly cost, keeps a price history, and tells me on Telegram about a new subscription or a price that went up.
- Renewal watch: when a Subscription changes, schedules a reminder at 9:00 two days before a trial ends or seven days before a yearly one renews; it's cancelled when the subscription is cancelling or cancelled.
- Renewal reminder: the scheduled reminder on Telegram, what, when and for how much.
- Review: on the 1st of every month at 9:00, and a 'Review' button on the list. What my trial and active subscriptions cost a month and a year per currency, the dearest, overlaps and ones my notes say I hardly use, written by the LLM, on Telegram.
- How to cancel: a 'How to cancel' button on an active Subscription. The LLM writes the steps and the date to cancel by, on Telegram, and it moves to cancelling. Nothing is ever paid or cancelled for me.
notes: Renewal reminder fires in a few minutes when the reminder time has passed but the date hasn't; monthly renewals aren't reminded. Price history is a stepped chart on the view page. The list groups by status with monthly totals.

name: Tables: row counts and growth alerts
description:
I want a Tables App that watches how my database's tables grow. Each Table is identified by its name and has its row count; pipelines write it, nothing is mine and I don't add them. On install it needs a database credential (a user that may only read), and Telegram.

One pipeline, Growth: every hour on the hour, and from a 'Count now' button on the Tables list, it counts the rows of the tables I name, saves the latest counts as the complete list of Tables, keeps a week of hourly counts as a history chart, and tells me on Telegram once when a table grows more than 3 times faster than usual, and once when it's back under 1.5 times.
notes: The SQL names example tables (orders, users) to replace; 'usual' is the median hourly growth over the last week (168 hourly points kept). The list shows a chart of the history above it, the view page charts one table's.

name: Tasks with tags, due dates and /task
description:
I want a Tasks App, no LLM: what I have to do. Each Task gets an id made automatically, so its title can change. It has a title, notes, a due date and tags (a list of words). I add tasks by hand on the list. Stages: open (where a task starts) and done; I move it from open to done and back, a pipeline never does. The list groups tasks by tag, with tag chips and a calendar of due days to filter by. It needs Telegram.

Pipelines:
- Due: every day at 7:00, the open tasks due today or overdue in one Telegram message, nothing if there are none.
- From Telegram: the Telegram command /task adds a task from the first line, every #word becoming a tag, and replies 'Added' with its title.
notes: The list also searches title, notes and tags and sorts by due date; the due column is highlighted a day ahead unless done. Old single-value tags read as one-item lists (M65).

name: Tenders scored against my profile, forms filled for me
description:
I want a Tenders App for open tenders and grant calls, scored against what my company does. A Profile is entirely mine, identified by its name: what we do, what we look for, and what isn't for us; I add it by hand, one is enough. A Tender is identified by its address; it has a title, buyer, deadline, budget, summary, score, why that score and source; the notes are mine. Stages: new (where it starts), prepared, submitted, won, lost, skipped. New to prepared by me or a pipeline; new or prepared to submitted or skipped by me only; submitted to won or lost by me; skipped, won or lost back to new by me. It needs the portal's recipe tenders.example/search, the LLM, and my Profile.

One pipeline, Tenders: every weekday at 7:00, and from a 'Check now' button on the list. It takes the portal's open calls in the software and consulting categories and the grants.example feed, keeps only the ones not seen before, reads each one's buyer, deadline and budget, scores it 0 to 100 against my Profile, and saves them. The ones scoring 50 or more wait for me to pick which to apply to. For each I pick, it finds the application form and proposes the values from my profile and my stored company-profile document; I approve or edit them, then it fills the form in the browser and stops before submitting, so I press the final button. Those become prepared. Only tenders.example and grants.example, at most 5 forms filled a day.
notes: The portal recipe reads up to 200 calls and the feed 100; a call whose form can't be found is skipped and stays new. The form's message field is 'why we fit, 3-4 sentences'.

name: Trips with bookings from email, reminders and briefings
description:
I want a Trips App. A Trip is entirely mine, identified by its name (like 'Lisbon, May 2027'): a destination city, start and end dates and notes; I type my trips in, pipelines only read them. A Booking is identified by its booking reference, so a change to it updates the same one; it has a title, kind (flight, train, bus, hotel, car, event, other), provider, start and end times, place, the trip it belongs to, price and currency, and the email's sender and subject. Stages: booked (where it starts) and cancelled, moved either way by me or a pipeline. It needs my trips added, an email account, the LLM, Google Calendar and Telegram.

Pipelines:
- Bookings: every 30 minutes, reads the last week's email, keeps booking confirmations, changes and cancellations, reads each, matches it to one of my trips, and saves it (a cancellation moves it to cancelled). Each new booking goes into my calendar after I approve, and Telegram tells me about it.
- Booking reminders: when a Booking is added or changes, schedules its reminder a day before it starts; a cancelled one's reminder is cancelled.
- Booking reminder: the scheduled Telegram message with its time, place and reference.
- Countdown: when I add a Trip or change its dates, schedules its briefing for 9:00 three days before it starts.
- Briefing: the scheduled briefing on Telegram, with the destination's forecast from Open-Meteo, the trip's bookings and what looks missing, written by the LLM.
- Packing list: a 'Packing list' button on a Trip; the LLM writes a packing list from the trip, its notes and its bookings, on Telegram.
notes: The Trip list page has no add flag although Trip is mine and setup says trips are added on its page. Bookings list groups by trip with price totals. The briefing only reaches Open-Meteo's geocoding and forecast hosts. The calendar approval is the calendar step's built-in gate (every side effect waits), not a separate gate step.

name: Cold weather
description: Every hour, on the hour, get the forecast for Sofia for the next 12 hours from Open-Meteo (it's free, no key) and find the lowest temperature and the hour it happens. Email me at me@example.com once when it will drop below 10°, and once more when it's back at 12° or over. While it stays cold, don't send one every hour. The email should give the lowest temperature in the next 12 hours and its hour. As always, the email waits for my approval before it goes out.
notes: Only api.open-meteo.com is allowed (policy.allowedDomains); the exact Open-Meteo URL with Sofia's coordinates and the email subject wording are details a person wouldn't spell out.

name: Daily digest
description: Every evening at 7, send me a Telegram digest of the last 24 hours: what ran, what waits for me and what failed.

name: Email follow-ups
description: On weekdays at 9:00, look through the emails I sent in the last 30 days and find the ones nobody answered in 5 days, the five waiting longest at a time. Each email gets a nudge proposed only once, even when I reject it: keep the ones proposed in a list of mine. For each, draft a short, friendly nudge of two or three sentences and send it as a reply in the same thread, to the person I wrote to and from the account I sent the original from. Each follow-up waits for my approval. No more than 10 follow-ups a day.
notes: email.awaiting remembers nothing (M71): the pipeline keeps the proposed emails in a collection (data.save) and leaves them out with data.dedupe against it. Writing in a thread again is a new email, so it can be nudged again.

name: Interview invites
description: Every 15 minutes, check my inbox for mail from the last two days that invites me to an interview, a call or a meeting about a job or project at a time they name. Mail that just asks when I'm free doesn't count. From each invitation, pick out when it starts, the company, the role and the address or video link. Look at my Google Calendar for what else is on in that hour, and write me short prep notes (who's inviting me, the role, what to prepare and ask, plus any clash). Then propose a calendar event "Interview: <company> (<role>)" at that time, with the place and the notes. Each event waits for my approval.
notes: Needs an email account and Google Calendar connected. Up to 50 messages per fetch; the event length used for the clash check is 60 minutes; the description also ends with the sender and subject of the email.

name: Live view check
description: A pipeline I start by hand to check that the live browser works: it opens Google's public reCAPTCHA demo page (https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api2/demo) in the visible browser and hands the page over to me. I solve the CAPTCHA in the run's live view, press Submit, and then Continue. It doesn't sign in anywhere.
notes: One step only: it opens the page headed with a 60-second timeout; the handover to the person happens because the CAPTCHA is detected, not because of a separate step.

name: Price watch
description: Every day at 10:00, read a shop's product list with my recipe for shop.example/hdd (up to 100 products, each with its link, title and price). Remember every product's price by its link, day by day. When any product got cheaper, send me a Telegram message starting with "Cheaper today:", one line per product: its title, the old price → the new price, "lowest so far" if it is, and its link. If nothing got cheaper, don't do anything.
notes: Prices are kept in a history collection named prices. The Telegram step has no when: condition, so on a day with nothing cheaper it may still send just the heading; the comment's intent is a message only when something got cheaper.

name: Product watch
description: Every day at 9:00, check the price of products I chose on their own shop pages, in my size and color. For now, the Fjällräven Skogsö padded jacket at https://www.bergfreunde.eu/fjaellraeven-skogsoe-padded-jacket-casual-jacket/ in size M, color Black. It should only be allowed to reach www.bergfreunde.eu. Remember each product's price. When one got cheaper, send me a Telegram message "Cheaper today:" with one line each: title and size/color, old → new price with currency, "lowest so far" if so, "sold out" if it's out of stock, and the link. If a page can't be read, send me a separate Telegram message saying which.
notes: No recipe: it reads the page's product data, falling back to the browser and a cheap model. Prices are kept per product id in a history collection named product-prices.

name: Recruiter replies (M4)
description: Every 15 minutes, read my new emails. Keep only those where a recruiter, hiring manager or client writes to me personally about a role, a project, an interview or a contract and expects an answer; skip job alerts, newsletters, notifications and mass mail, and leave any email that belongs to one of my topics to Topic replies, so nothing is answered twice. For each one, draft a short, warm reply as me: if it could fit, show interest and ask for what is missing (rate, remote or on-site, start date, duration) and propose a short call; if it clearly doesn't, decline politely in a sentence or two. I approve every reply before it goes out, as a reply in the same thread. At most 20 replies a day.

name: Topic replies
description: Every 15 minutes, fetch the new email from the last two days in all the mailboxes my topics read. Keep only mail from a person writing to me (or to a few of us) that expects a reply from me, not newsletters, receipts or mass mail. Sort it into my topics. For each email that belongs to a topic, draft a brief reply as me using what Storm knows about that topic and its documents: put a placeholder where they don't say, and agree to nothing new on my behalf. Send it to the sender, in the same thread, from the account it came to. Each reply waits for my approval, at most 20 a day. Leave email with no topic alone.
notes: Up to 50 messages per fetch. The draft uses the topic picked automatically (topic: auto). The Topics page can set this pipeline up itself (Answer your topics' email).

name: Topic tidy-up
description: Every Sunday at 7:00, tidy up what Storm knows about my topics. For any topic that has collected more facts than a reply draft has room for, propose merging facts that are parts of one thing and retiring facts that no longer hold, like a date that has passed or a status a later fact overtook. Show me the proposals for review so I can pick which ones to do, and only apply the ones I chose.
notes: Disputed facts are left alone, topics whose facts all fit aren't read, and proposals I leave out aren't proposed again. All of that is the step's own behaviour. The Topics page can set this up (Tidy up topics' facts).

name: Topic upkeep
description: Every 15 minutes, keep my topics' memory up to date. Fetch the new email from the last two days in all the mailboxes my topics read, set aside newsletters, notifications, receipts and other automated mail, and keep what people wrote to me. Also fetch what I sent in the last two days. Sort both into my topics and collect the attachments of the matched emails. Check each topic's GitHub repositories and Google Drive folders for changed files and index them for my drafts to quote. Then propose the facts worth remembering from the emails and changed files, let me pick which go in for review, and save only those to the topics' memory.
notes: The triage step is marked answerable: false (these are not reply candidates). The Topics page can set this up (Keep topics up to date).
